6. Policymakers can respond to a ﬁnancial crisis in three ways. First, they
can use conventional monetary and ﬁscal policy to expand aggregate
demand. Second, the central bank can provide liquidity by acting as a
lender of last resort. Third, policymakers can use public funds to prop
up the ﬁnancial system.
7. Preventing ﬁnancial crises is not easy, but policymakers have tried to reduce
the likelihood of future crises by focusing more on regulating shadow
banks, by restricting the size of ﬁnancial ﬁrms, by trying to limit excessive
risk taking, by reforming the regulatory agencies that oversee the ﬁnancial
system, and by taking a more macroeconomic perspective when regulating
ﬁnancial institutions.
